W2 (empirical), after E015. Best is E015: 6.578 s, 0.7574 (E010 recipe plus CUDA-graph capture of the train step). The margin over the 0.753 bar is about 0.44 pp.

Measured (3 seeds, all complete): E001 9ep eager 0.7430/9.43. E004 compiled 0.7486/9.04. E005 +EMA 0.7583/9.10. E006 +Muon 0.7649/9.45. E007 +prog-res 0.7590/7.33. E008 8.5ep 0.7572/6.98. E009 LR floor 0 0.7564/6.99. E010 width 512 0.7548/6.64. E011 aggressive res 0.7451/5.70. E012 exact rerun of E010: bit-identical accuracy, time within 0.1%. E013 LS 0.2: 0.7551. E014 Muon lr x1.5: 0.7557. E015 CUDA graphs: 0.7574/6.578.

Mechanisms:
1. Epoch dial: -0.5 epoch costs about 0.18 pp and saves about 4.8% time, roughly linear.
2. Compile saves about 4%.
3. EMA/Lookahead: +0.97 pp for +0.06 s. The cheapest gain seen.
4. Muon: +0.66 pp for +0.35 s.
5. Progressive resizing: -22% time for -0.59 pp. Time tracks pixel count.
6. Width 576 to 512: -4.8% time for -0.25 pp, about the epoch-dial exchange rate.
7. Resolution cliff (E011): -14% time for -1.4 pp.
8. Loss and optimizer-scale knobs (LS, Muon lr, LR floor) are flat within noise. Hyperparameters sit on a plateau.
9. CUDA graphs: only -0.9% time, so the run is compute-bound, not launch-bound. The +0.26 pp accuracy change is reshuffle noise, since the math is nominally identical (probably RNG or ordering differences).
10. Noise: runs are deterministic per seed. Seed and recipe-reshuffle noise is about ±0.2 pp on 3-seed means. Time noise is about 0.5%. Fixed costs are about 0.3-0.5 s.

Misses: I under-predicted EMA, Muon and resizing, and over-predicted E009 and E011 accuracy. Lesson: accuracy-neutral knobs land within ±0.2 pp of the current value, and time stays put unless pixels or FLOPs change.

Unsure: how much of the remaining 6.6 s is fixed cost (data to GPU, whitening, augmentation) versus per-step compute. Whether weight decay matters with only 25 steps per epoch. Whether plain EMA matches Lookahead. The held-out seed spread.

With 0.44 pp of slack, the real lever is spending it on epochs, about 1 epoch, which would save about 9%.

forecasts.reason: Weight decay is probably near a plateau like the other knobs; time is unchanged and the accuracy shift is within noise.
CUDA graphs already removed launch overhead for only 0.9%, so remaining breaks and syncs give little more than 1%; the GPU is mostly busy.
Lookahead's resetting of the fast weights likely contributes beyond endpoint averaging; plain EMA probably recovers less than the full 1 pp and lands about 0.2 pp lower.

cruxes: What fraction of the 6.6 s is fixed non-epoch cost (data upload, whitening eigh, augmentation, first-step effects) versus per-step GPU compute? If fixed cost is large, cutting epochs gains less than 4.8% per 0.5 epoch.
Is the E015 accuracy gain (0.7574 vs 0.7548) a real effect of graph capture or just reshuffle noise? This sets how much slack remains for cutting epochs.
Does plain EMA match Lookahead's reset-to-slow-weights behavior? That decides whether averaging can be simplified or improved.
